question: Which low-dimensional task similarities and capacity ratios determine transfer, forgetting, and interference in sequentially trained wide neural networks?

key_findings.claim: Single-head short-term forgetting decomposes into a competition between relevant-feature overlap and rule overlap.
key_findings.evidence: The solvable Gibbs-posterior model yields F = 2(gamma_RF - gamma_rule), separating whether tasks reuse input features from whether they assign compatible outputs.

key_findings.claim: Multi-head continual learning has a load-dependent phase transition that separates fixed-representation, generalizing, and overfitting regimes.
key_findings.evidence: For load alpha=P/N below one, representations can remain fixed with zero forgetting; above one, sufficiently dissimilar tasks enter a regime with zero old-task forgetting but divergent new-task error, termed catastrophic anterograde interference.

key_findings.claim: The theoretical critical loads track controlled MNIST task-pair experiments, but require highly symmetric task relations.
key_findings.evidence: Permuted/split MNIST examples show transitions near predicted critical alpha values (about 1.51 and 3.19 for two reported similarities), while the derivation assumes uniform regularization and symmetric pairwise task statistics.

method.core_idea: Solve sequential learning in infinite-width deep ReLU networks through statistical-mechanics order parameters for task relationship and data load.
method.mechanism: A Gibbs posterior with L2 perturbation regularization produces saddle-point equations; scalar feature, rule, input-subspace, and representation similarities define phase boundaries and forgetting errors.
assumptions: Networks are sufficiently wide for the thermodynamic approximation.
Tasks have symmetric, controllable pairwise relationships and labeled task identity in the multi-head setting.
Uniform L2 distance to previous parameters is a meaningful proxy for continual-learning regularization.

techniques.role: Separates input feature, relevant feature, rule, and representation overlap.
Turns sequential learning into tractable saddle-point equations.
Maps capacity and task similarity to transfer and interference regimes.

evaluations.result: Simulations follow analytic curves across task-overlap parameters and network depth.

evaluations.setting: Permuted and split MNIST task pairs
evaluations.metric: Critical data load for phase transition
evaluations.result: Observed transitions are close to predicted critical loads for reported similarity settings.
Intermediate regularization can optimize the stability-plasticity tradeoff.

limitations: The analysis relies on wide-network, Gibbs-posterior, and symmetric-task assumptions.
Multi-head results presume task identity and separate outputs, unlike task-free continual learning.
Uniform L2 perturbation regularization omits replay, sparsity, routing, and optimizer dynamics.
failure_modes: Zero measured forgetting can coexist with divergent learning on the new task.
A single aggregate task similarity can hide incompatible feature and rule relationships.
Predicted phase boundaries may shift in finite, convolutional, transformer, or asymmetric task sequences.
reusable_insights: Continual-learning evaluation should measure forward interference as well as backward forgetting.
Task relatedness should be factorized into feature reuse and label-rule compatibility.
Capacity-normalized load can reveal abrupt regime changes hidden by mean accuracy.
open_questions: Can empirical estimators recover the order parameters from real pretrained representations?
How do replay, parameter-efficient adapters, or sparse routing reshape the phase diagram?
Can the theory handle heterogeneous task graphs and order effects over many tasks?

competitive_landscape.title: Overcoming catastrophic forgetting in neural networks
competitive_landscape.difference: EWC protects parameters using Fisher importance; this paper derives phase behavior for a simpler L2 perturbation prior and explicitly separates task-relation order parameters.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Curves for Continual Learning in Neural Networks: Self-Knowledge Transfer and Forgetting
competitive_landscape.difference: The NTK learning-curve analysis studies transfer and forgetting in a lazy regime; the present work permits feature learning and identifies load-driven phases in deep wide networks.

competitive_landscape.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Continual Learning: A Neural Tangent Kernel Perspective
competitive_landscape.difference: That work analyzes PEFT through NTKs; this paper focuses on statistical-mechanics order parameters and phase transitions under shared or multi-head full-network adaptation.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: catastrophic-forgetting regularizers and NTK learning curves are established. The distinctive result is a compact feature/rule/load parameterization that exposes an anterograde-interference phase where retention alone is misleading.
reviewer_notes: Main derivations, phase diagrams, MNIST checks, depth analysis, and discussion were read. Primary competitor records checked 2026-08-23. Applicability outside the solvable wide-network model is an open empirical question.
